cyberattack: Other: Encoded-path redirect bypass; security-boundary significance unconfirmed
data.description: Ordinary OJJDP EZAUCR paths repeatedly redirected to a replacement page, while encoded parent-directory paths returned the legacy statistics application and real public arrest tables. One same-window comparison has a normal redirect at 20:19:35 and an encoded-path response at 20:19:38 on May 30. Retrieved data include Lincoln County, Maine juvenile counts and US statistics for 2008–2014. The investigation verified all 16 distinct response bodies behind 18 encoded-path captures. This demonstrates a path-dependent routing difference, but the contemporaneous security purpose of the redirect, requester/session continuity and AI identity are unknown.
data.summary: Archived May requests reached a legacy Justice Department arrest-statistics tool through encoded parent-directory paths while ordinary URLs redirected. Public data was retrieved. The records do not establish a security-control violation or identify an AI requester.
